Reviewed head: `a8843cca75ff29d51aa7b288c80b8bdc3a1ca3bb`. TeX SHA-256: `f2d70e6963708f4f380f35d302896ad3c8700d22d1fd4d6d886db52bcad6c9c2`; supplied PDF SHA-256: `367bd75c7f5f52d7e507a7ce203ad9121cd6511c828c2718793d43f5585dd4d1`.

The manuscript contains historical-review references, so this was not a blind review. Run metadata is not provider-signed model attestation or protected-App approval.

Two concrete corrections are needed:

1. **M1 prints the wrong normalization.** At [TeX line 2506](https://github.com/elliotglazer/diophantine-z-q/blob/a8843cca75ff29d51aa7b288c80b8bdc3a1ca3bb/research/quartic214-manuscript/quartic214.tex#L2506), also PDF p.85, `a_sigma=D(mu_sigma)^{-1}/4` means reciprocal degree divided by four. With `mu_1=1`, this gives `a_1=1/4`, contradicting the next cocycle identity already at `(1,1)`. The intended exponent `-1/4` is correctly printed in [H1](https://github.com/elliotglazer/diophantine-z-q/blob/a8843cca75ff29d51aa7b288c80b8bdc3a1ca3bb/research/quartic214-manuscript/quartic214.tex#L3071). We read the original Markdown argument and compared the other quarter-root occurrences: the intended derivation exists. This is an inconsistent notation/serialization issue affecting the representation's definition, not newly missing arithmetic. Correct the source ambiguity, TeX and PDF together.
2. **A degree product became a subscript.** [Line 2812](https://github.com/elliotglazer/diophantine-z-q/blob/a8843cca75ff29d51aa7b288c80b8bdc3a1ca3bb/research/quartic214-manuscript/quartic214.tex#L2812) prints `sum e_{{jf_j}}=d`; the needed identity is `sum_j e_j f_j=d`. The correct derivation already appears earlier in the same argument. Correct the occurrence and check related serialized indices/products. This does not refute the different estimate.

Within our stated scope, the following checks were positive:

- The exact sparse checker passed: twenty changed factor identities, six inverse-weight relations, 162 unchanged rows, the 214-coordinate/188-row quartic table, and 21 corruption controls. The H4 rational numeric certificate also passed with four negative controls. Computations were serial and capped at 1 GiB. Deterministic TeX regeneration passed, illustrating that reproducibility alone does not catch the two semantic defects above.
- I reconstructed the changed valuation minima, trace/pole inequality, integrality-before-logarithm-congruence argument, and resulting separate radical divisibilities. These joins work with the stated recovered root/scalar objects. The uniform soundness algebra correctly uses `14/9<2`; neither it nor the coefficient check provides a numerical defining member at `N=53`.
- The existence reviewer checked the actual sum-aggregate application and P08–P20 choice/threshold interfaces against the internal arguments and [published Von Buhren Theorem 1.1](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/jtnb.981.pdf). The input-dependent prime data are fixed before the auxiliary analytic limit; no extra uniform prime estimate is consumed.
- The height reviewer checked the operative repeated-factor product construction in [published Gaudron–Rémond (2023), pp.97–98](https://smf.emath.fr/system/files/filepdf/smf_mem_176_0.pdf), and the dimension-two isogeny specialization. No new arithmetic defect was found in that intended averaging join. It remains conditional on the identified geometric/modular/height inputs.

Each lane froze its source-use reconstruction before reconciling with declared contracts. This was **not** a recursive audit of all 703 pages. Full source checks remain outstanding in the rank/RC/Kato and Gaussian-prime/GI/transference foundations, the changed Version16 foundation application, and parts of the geometric, p-adic, integral-model and metric height chain. We did not exhaust the historical objection corpus. These are review limitations, not claims that unread premises are false or unproved.

Accordingly, correcting the two formulas alone would not establish full acceptance. This report supplies scoped mathematical checks and adverse findings; it supplies **no complete-proof, complete-inventory, release or protected-App approval**. No reviewed file was changed.

# Independent follow-up review of PR30

Reviewer: `/root/q214_astra_repair_review`, nonauthor internal model reviewer requested as `gpt-6-astra`, 12 November 2026. Final artifact review of the held author candidate; the publication note above supplies the exact commit and independent public readback.

## Decisions

**Complete assembled-proof acceptance: not accepted. Complete mathematical inventory acceptance: not accepted. Full Protocol D closure: incomplete. Trusted controller eligibility: not attested.** This review does not certify the proposed arithmetic theorem or supply the required protected-App approval.

The held receiving corrections F1–F5 are resolved at the bounded scope below. I accept only **formula-incorporation**, **related-use-coverage**, **source-inclusion-and-changed-joins**, and **research-artifact-packaging**. These scopes mean the exact repaired expressions, the explicitly searched failure classes, selected source transport/current changed interfaces, and the bound research artifacts. They do not mean all formulas, all prerequisites, every historical objection or every PDF page have been reviewed. The complete-proof and inventory decisions remain separate negative acceptance decisions caused by incomplete review coverage, not a mathematical disproof.

## Conditions and scope

The human requested automated repairs, independent Astra checking and a full follow-up report posted verbatim. The task supplied the repository, protocols, resource limits, previous adverse review locations and the identities of F1/F2. It supplied no desired mathematical verdict. I read actual source proofs before consulting declared inventories or prior report bodies; the initial table is preserved separately. The source prose itself includes earlier review references. This review was therefore not blind. No human drafted or edited this report in the interaction I observed. That observation cannot establish absence of all human or shared-model influence. Requested model metadata is not provider-signed authentication or approval by the protected controller.

I authored review evidence and findings only. I reported F3/F4/F5 to the separate Sol author lane without editing the proof or author contracts. Component reviewers are separate fresh nonauthor tasks, each with its own source-first table: `v16_foundations` and `d210_modularity`. Distinct task identities do not eliminate correlated errors. The initial source-use table is deliberately a coarse dependency reconstruction, not a representation that all 703 pages were recursively audited.

The baseline is commit a8843cca75ff29d51aa7b288c80b8bdc3a1ca3bb. The original adverse report is preserved at research/quartic214-manuscript-review/audits/astra-a8843cc-20261112/. Its two findings and explicit coverage limits remain part of this review. Earlier favorable reports are evidence at their exact versions and scopes, not acceptance of the new renderer or revised receiving manuscript.

## Findings and historical disposition

F1 concerns the normalization of the quasi-isogenies. The adjacent original prose specifies a positive fourth root and the next cocycle equation requires it. From degree multiplicativity, D(mu_sigma)D(mu_tau)=c(sigma,tau)^4D(mu_sigma_tau). With a_sigma=D(mu_sigma)^(-1/4), positivity gives a_sigma a_tau/a_sigma_tau=1/abs(c). The identity element gives a_1=1. The original rendered reciprocal-then-divide-by4 failed this case. Thus earlier intended justification exists; this is an inconsistent serialization, not a newly absent arithmetic theorem. The inspected first repair printed the complete exponent correctly at TeX2506/PDF 85. The final held TeX/PDF retain this correction; F1 is resolved at this receiving scope.

The normalization is consumed by t_sigma=a_sigma/b(sigma), with coboundary of b equal to c/abs(c). It yields the genuine representation, equal to the actual Tate module on G_Lprime because mu,a,b are all1 there. The fourth exterior power uses a_sigma^4D(mu_sigma)=1, so det rho=b^-4 kappa². I checked these immediate consumers in M2/M6/H1. This does not independently supply their geometric and modularity premises.

F2 concerns the local degree sum. The original height-different section1 already proves rank(U_j)=e_jf_j by the uniformizer filtration, using full residue degrees, including inseparable degree. All complete components occur, so their ranks sum to d. The later repeated use malformed the product into an index. Multiplying the component bound r_j<=e_j-1+e_jA by f_j yields sum f_jr_j<=d(1+A)-sum f_j<=d(1+A). The same C=B/(t-2)B is consumed by the height argument. Earlier justification exists and the first repaired PDF 98 prints the full product. The final held TeX/PDF retain this correction; F2 is resolved at this receiving scope.

The related-use review found two additional inconsistent notations in that first repair candidate. F3: relative-extension labels in height-different31/65/83/85 printed D_U/V, trace_U/W and relative r/e indices with the slash outside the subscript. The preserved evaluation source357–404 prints the relative different correctly and supplies the same tower argument. F4: numeric suffixes immediately preceding Unicode powers escaped numeric-index conversion: C2²/A3²/etc. in the changed factors, s1²/s2² in reciprocal equations, and c4³ in the modular j formula. The uniform-existence factor duplicate and the literal factor-extraction TeX already supply the intended formulas. These were reported for author correction. F5 was then found in the revised torsion paragraph: the Markdown emphasis parser consumed the pullback star in [n]^*omega=n omega and the ungrouped [n] index lost its n. The other located mathematical stars (raw TeX a_i^*, alpha^*E, Q_11^* and the explicit metric pushforward) were preserved. This was reported separately before any final acceptance. All five corrections were subsequently compared in the final held TeX and actual PDF. F3/F4/F5 are resolved at this receiving scope. The final nineteen source-line overlays include the combined F3/F5 derivative line. All these findings concerned supplied arguments whose earlier representations disagreed; they are not counterexamples to the intended arithmetic. FINDINGS.json preserves the exact first-candidate hashes and sites.

The search scope comes from the failure mechanisms: all 19 selected Markdown inputs, all rational-power/slash cases, numeric suffixes followed by superscripts, relative extension indices and the degree-product sums; the immediate repeated definitions and consumers; and corresponding selected TeX sources. Unchanged V16 text is separately transported exactly. This is bounded semantic review, not a claim to identify every possible serialization error throughout703 pages.

## Arithmetic composition checked

I read the assembly, existence, uniform-existence, local factor source, all height bridge proofs and modularity argument, with component extension of current foundation and geometry checks. The local extraction has pairwise distinct finite term valuation classes. The constant term supplies minimum<=0; zero tests simply remove terms. For the five factors, the selected trace/pole place gives ell>-nu/2, hence the required test depths. Positive even reciprocal valuations precede the formal logarithm argument, so its relative error is used as an absolute congruence only after ratio integrality is established. This produces M_j³|Delta and M_j|J separately, with no extra scalar or product divisibility between the two scales.

The full-family height bound is applied to both transformed rational arguments, including the small-height/radical-one branch. Their inverse projective row bounds are3 and7; outside fixed Sigma the two contact blocks are disjoint, giving exponent7/6. The aggregate theorem concerns a sum, not the unused odd-label product theorem; its output is B²<=M1 h(T)+M2 for the actual quarter-trace. With Delta nonzero the exponent is14/9<2. The scalar lower growth therefore forces Delta=0 uniformly for sufficiently large N. The Lucas lower bound then contradicts the J-nonzero upper bound after the fixed coefficient149^-L_N is small enough. Integrality of51x²+2504 forces x integral because51 is squarefree. These algebraic joins do not make the threshold effective.

Completeness fixes its uniform scalar threshold before the input-dependent labels and finite progressions. The coefficients of both contact scales are cleared and equal coefficients merged with incidences preserved before the prime theorem. All those data may depend on (N,x), but are fixed before the auxiliary analytic limit. The new factor exponents are checked again at the fresh witnesses; old pole coordinates are not reused. The resulting pole inputs have the required square denominator, positivity and local depths. RC applies to the actual non-CM curve y²=x(x-l)(x+3l), separately for the two positive squarefree11mod12 parameters, and uses full Selmer corank before rank/finite-Sha. The CM index curve is a distinct object. The V16 component reviewed these receiving joins while leaving the full RC machinery unreviewed.

## Expanded height-source review

The integral evaluation, different, metric and assembly proofs were read completely. I reconstructed the trace-lattice finiteness argument, finite flatness on the normal surface over the regular two-dimensional base, codimension-one descent from a common regular blowup, extension by reflexivity, trace-normalized finite duality, and specialization at t=2. The result is the literal evaluation vector in the trace dual of the nonmaximal order C, not the maximal order and not an unspecified scalar multiple. Hom base change is justified by finite projectivity despite the nonflat specialization. The projected overlattice length bound keeps every coordinate subset available.

Primary statements checked directly include Stacks00R4,0BFP,0AHI,0BUL,0ATX,0AVT and0BW2/3/E/F/G/J, with their required Noetherian, flat, LCI and normality assumptions matched to these constructions. [Final published Javanpeykar 2014](https://msp.org/ant/2014/8-1/ant-v8-n1-p04-s.pdf) §§2.1/2.3, Lemma2.3.1 proof and §4.1 were read for the original metric, positive exceptional twist and imperfect-residue different estimate. The project’s elementary reconstructions preserve those conventions. The torsion derivative is N rather than N²; normalization reverses trace-dual inclusions; tower transitivity passes the bound to each intermediate point field. All completed components enter the discriminant sum. The primitive torsion quotient gives the same modular curve, and p|N uses finite flat torsion rather than an open model that inverted N.

For the analytic bound, Belyi degree exceeds2g-2, so evaluation has full rank at the distinct fibre points. One coordinate minor over K works at every embedding. The radius 1/2 mean-value estimate and Hadamard give the determinant bound; the integral determinant section gives the height inequality with the correct sign. The auxiliary splitting/semistability field cancels in normalized height and is never substituted for Lprime in the surface-isogeny bound.

The operative product averaging proof was compared to [final published GR 2023](https://smf.emath.fr/system/files/filepdf/smf_mem_176_0.pdf) proof of Lemma 16.2(1), printed 98, and Theorem 1.9(1), printed 7–8. Its same-field product has no larger original stable height and may repeat simple factors. The A^r subobject forces r separate occurrences; the complement lower bound and product additivity provide one small surface, then the dimension-two isogeny points from that surface to A over the same Lprime. This yields exactly H3.1. The superseded quotient route is not accepted by this comparison. The final 2022 Rémond body remains an indirect source-access limitation. Primary-source details and explicit derivations are in EVIDENCE.md; source bytes were not locally reacquired where shell DNS failed, so web-access observations are not falsely assigned local hashes.

## Current V16 and other component work

The V16 component reconstructed the changed horizontal normalization, fixed-E Tao–Ziegler adaptation, normalized GI-to-Gaussian join and pole/RC consumer domain. It checked actual current proof passages and selected published GTZ/TZ statements, and read the exact prior fixed-E argument plus precision addendum as derivations. Eleven inspected excerpts match the integrated manuscript after documented LF and navigation-anchor handling. It found no new defect within that scope. Its report explicitly excludes complete RC/Kato, Gaussian TypeI/II, full GI induction and obstruction-tail prerequisite review. Exact text transport does not close those obligations. The D210/modularity component has now completed a separately frozen source-first review. It read the actual full-three D210 geometry, all-Hom descent, normalized lift, modularity, five-to-three comparison and conductor/quotient joins. Direct published checks included Calegari's geometric modularity statement, Deligne–Serre primitive extraction, Carayol's full theorem (including the dyadic case), selected Milne canonical-model criteria and Silverberg–Zarhin full 11 semistability. It reconstructed the regular-torsor degree divisibility576, B-linear isogenies of the actual fiber surfaces, the relative p-Frobenius trace comparison and the r5/r3 coverage of every residue prime. No invalid inference was established in that bounded lane. Its report explicitly leaves PEL classification, parts of the tame model, p-adic/Faltings/Kato prerequisites, Shimura quotient/twist and several ramification sources unclosed. Milne 1986 was image-only with unsuccessful image access; no direct inspection is claimed. These are partial source checks, not blanket acceptance of six modularity contracts or the final receiving TeX. See [the D210 component report](https://github.com/elliotglazer/diophantine-z-q/blob/e3626cac202cdbcdfedc2bff1978dcd3ea3fd3ab/research/quartic214-manuscript-review/current-astra-20261112/d210/REPORT.md) and its exact source-use/binding records.

Full mathematical inventory coverage and final assembled-proof closure are not established by this review. Outstanding coverage includes extensive inherited RC/Kato/Gaussian/GI arguments, transitive geometry/p-adic/comparison prerequisites beyond the stated component reading, the complete historical objection corpus and exhaustive semantic/visual serialization. These are identified limitations of what was reviewed, not assertions that unread theorems are false or missing. ## Horizontal normalization

Primary source inspected: Green–Tao–Ziegler, *An inverse theorem for the Gowers U^{s+1}[N]-norm*, Annals176(2012),1231–1372, DOI10.4007/annals.2012.176.2.11, publisher PDF https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v176-n2-p11-p.pdf . Direct readings: normalized interval definition p1232; Def9.6 and following additivity p1281–82; CorB.4 p1334; LemB.9 p1337. They supply horizontal quotient conventions, additive horizontal Taylor map and polynomial product/Taylor properties. The full general inverse theorem is not substituted for the local repaired proof.

Current construction takes the horizontal discrepancy in the image of Gamma intersect G_(i,1), chooses its internal preimage, and right-multiplies by its negative binomial power. Each correction is lattice-valued pointwise; fixed-order product remains lattice-valued, so the actual represented orbit is identical. In the ordinary filtration it is polynomial because the coefficient belongs to the required filtered group; product closure applies. In horizontal weight i, its binomial i-th difference subtracts precisely the discrepancy. Other weights contribute zero to the corresponding horizontal quotients. Thus the conclusion is a real-vector equality before changing lattice, not merely an equality in the old torus.

The small-coordinate test is globally defined through a cutoff on a circle lift and remains unit-valued; the central top image keeps its vertical character. Rational-coordinate removal passes to a finite covering lattice and residue interpolation has disjoint supports with sum of squared weights1. Its actual sequence is the original padded by zero, so fixed projection recovers it. Raising remaining letters to M-th powers and dividing the SAME real lifts preserves their summed horizontal vectors identically.
